messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-98432 - prometheus_scrape_failure on metrics-scrape-cluster - severity: P1

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-98432 has been triggered and notified the on-call rotation (team: eng-sre). Escalation: 10m -> 30m.

erin chen: saw this, paging on-call. I can take the first look. Prometheus scrape errors spiking for `metrics-scrape-cluster` across eu-west and us-west. Logs showing 503 from scrape endpoints.

mohit singh: acked the PD. I'm on-call. brief: are we seeing traffic spikes or just scrape target failures?

erin chen: no traffic spike on exporter side, looks like scrape targets return 503 for `/metrics` or time out. example from scrape pod logs: 
```
level=error msg="fetch error" target="10.12.5.8:9100" err="Get \"http://10.12.5.8:9100/metrics\": net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)"
```

rachel kim: also seeing a bunch of 5xx from the log-ingest side. Kibana query for `log_ingest_rate` shows backlog up ~4x last hour. Might be correlated.

maxwell lee: pinging infra team to check if any kube nodes in those AZs are unhealthy. @ops-team please chime in if you see node replacement or network changes.

ops-team: (system) no node replacements in the last 2 hours. No rolling upgrades scheduled. Network team: no infra events reported.

mohit singh: running quick checks - `kubectl get pods -n monitoring -l app=prom-scrape -o wide` shows scrapers are Restarting on 3 pods. Could be memory pressure. I'll grab logs.

erin chen: FYI customer impact: internal dashboards using `redwood.system.*` metrics will show gaps; some customer SLO monitoring that relies on host-exporter metrics may alert. Not seeing direct user-facing feature outages yet, but metric-backed alerts will bounce.

sre-runbook-bot: Runbook suggested for prom-scrape failures: 1) Check scrapers pod memory/oom 2) Check prometheus target statuses 3) Restart scrapers if stuck 4) Apply temp scrape-reduce if needed. Link: https://redwood.confluence/sre/runbooks/prometheus-scrape-failures

mohit singh: logs from prom-scrape pod:
```
OOMKilled process: collector heap exceeded 1.9GB
panic: runtime: out of memory
```

erin chen: that confirms OOMs. Likely a recent exporter version or payload change causing higher memory. Options: increase memory, roll back exporter, or reduce scrape cardinality. What's quickest?

rachel kim: log ingest backlog suggests downstream consumers impacted if scrapers slow. If we scale scrapers up with >memory it may help short-term. I can temporarily scale `prom-scrape` to 6 replicas (currently 3) and bump mem to 2Gi.

mohit singh: doing that now. command: `kubectl scale deployment prom-scrape -n monitoring --replicas=6` and `kubectl set resources deployment/prom-scrape -n monitoring --limits=memory=2Gi --requests=1Gi`

(30s later)

mohit singh: scaled to 6, updated resources. New pods are coming up. Watching logs.

erin chen: monitoring Prometheus `target` page — some targets are moving from DOWN -> UP after restart. Still seeing a subset failing with 503s from exporter endpoints in eu-west-3.

maxwell lee: checking k8s events in eu-west cluster: some nodes reported kube-proxy flapping earlier, might cause transient 503s. Ops says proxy restart series happened 8m ago. Might be root cause of connection resets and timeouts.

rachel kim: log ingest backlog stabilized a bit (down 35% in last 10m) but still elevated. Not clearing yet.

mohit singh: prom targets status now: 120/136 up -> 130/136 up after scale. 6 targets still DOWN. I'll exec into one of the failing exporter pods to curl `/metrics`.

mohit singh: inside pod curl shows `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable` and exporter logs show `rate limited` errors to internal dependency (a proc that reads cgroups) — weird. Maybe a kernel parameter or container limit kicked in.

erin chen: possible cgroup v2 limit or systemd issue after kube-proxy restarts. For immediate mitigation: add a prometheus scrape relabel to skip known flaky targets for the next 30m to avoid alert churn, and open action item to investigate exporters deeper.

rachel kim: agreed. I'll apply a temporary `relabel_config` to the prometheus scrape job to drop targets with label `region=eu-west-3` for 30m. Command I will run: 
```
# edit prometheus configmap
kubectl -n monitoring edit configmap prometheus-config
# add relabel to job_name: node
```
(doing it now)

(2m later)

rachel kim: applied temporary relabel for eu-west-3 on node exporter scrape job. Prometheus reload succeeded. Alerts for those targets should quiet in ~1m.

erin chen: marking customer impact: medium (internal dashboards degraded, some alerting noise). No direct user request failures. Notified Prod Support to expect noise.

pagerduty-bot: PD-98432 acknowledged by mohith singh (on-call). Escalation timer paused.

mohit singh: continuing root cause work — next steps: 1) check exporter binary version diffs 2) check kernel / cgroup logs on nodes 3) evaluate roll-back of exporter image if we see mismatch. I'll take ownership until 1800 UTC then hand off to next on-call.

erin chen: thanks. I'll open a ticket and post runbook steps in JIRA: SRE-6873. Also notifying customer success for any customers who rely on host metrics dashboards.

maxwell lee: ops confirmed kube-proxy restarts were from a mis-applied iptables rule by a network automation job at 17:12 UTC — rollback done. We're following up on why job touched prod clusters.

rachel kim: backlog for log-ingest is now trending down to near-normal after scale and relabel, but we'll need to ensure exporters not OOMing again. Suggest we pin exporter to previous known good image on scrapers and schedule a deeper postmortem.

mohit singh: note: I'll pin prom-scrape to `prom-exporter:1.4.2` (previous) and rollout 3 at a time. Command: `kubectl set image deploy/prom-scrape prom-exporter=ghcr.io/redwood/prom-exporter:1.4.2 -n monitoring`

(10m later)

mohit singh: rollouts in progress. New pods stable. OOM messages gone from logs for 20m. Targets up 136/136. Good signal.

erin chen: excellent. Customer impact now low. Logging backlog cleared to within 10% of baseline.

mohit singh: planning handoff — I'll be off rotation after 1800 UTC. Handoff notes: cause likely combo of kube-proxy flaps (network automation job) + exporter memory regression in latest image. Temporary mitigations: scale scrapers, relabel skip for eu-west-3, rollback exporter image. Actions for next shift: investigate exporter memory leak, audit network automation job, add alert for kube-proxy flapping.

sre-runbook-bot: Recommended post-incident items: postmortem within 72h, update runbook with exporter OOM checklist, add a synthetic check for `/metrics` latency.

erin chen: assigning postmortem to @rachel_k and @maxwell_lee. Please include timeline, why network job impacted kube-proxy, and repro steps for exporter OOM.

rachel kim: will take PM for postmortem. Creating doc SRE-PM-98432 and will loop in infra/security for network job audit.

pagerduty-bot: PD-98432 auto-resolve scheduled after incident closed. Please mark all mitigations and link postmortem in PD ticket.

mohit singh: handing off to @maxwell_lee at 1800 UTC. I'll post final status in the ticket.

maxwell lee: acked handoff. I'll monitor overnight and pick up postmortem coordination tomorrow. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

erin chen: closing thread for now — moving to incident channel for postmortem notes. Great quick work everyone.
